title: T-SPOnse: Therapy-associated changes in TSPO expression in the tumor microenvironment of glioma
summary: This observational study will examine a protein called TSPO (translocator protein) in primary brain tumors. This will be achieved using PET scans and special "PET tracers" that can detect and visualize this protein in patients. The results of the PET images will be compared with images from other common imaging methods (e.g., MRI and amino acid PET) and with results from tissue sample analyses. Furthermore, we will investigate how the expression of this protein changes over time during therapy and how it behaves when the tumor recurs. Our analyses aim to gain a deeper understanding of the role of TSPO in the tumor cells and in the tumor microenvironment including the immune cells in order to better predict aggressive disease courses and to detect treatment response or failure at an early stage.

interventions.name: Study participants will receive additional PET scans as part of the study: at the time of initial diagnosis, patients will receive a preoperative TSPO-PET (FET-PET as part of clinical routine). criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Suspected newly diagnosed glioma CNS-WHO Grade 2-4; signed informed consent; age ≥ 18 years.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients who are not eligible for tumor-specific therapy (radiation, chemotherapy, or radiochemotherapy depending on tumor type); patients who are unable to give informed consent due to an accompanying psychiatric disorder; known history of alcohol or drug abuse in the 12 months prior to screening; contraindications for magnetic resonance imaging (pacemaker or implanted metal in the skull) or PET imaging; pregnancy / breastfeeding.
